Default Title - $185.00 USD Quantity Add to Cart     Classic rectified octave-up fuzz with a Stank control that overloads the octaving circuit for positively filthy tones—not a polite octave doubler. Blend wet and dry, dial from shimmering octave fuzz to full stank. Hand-soldered in British Columbia for guitar and bass. ▶ Watch video demos Why fuzz players choose the Octave Fuzz with Stank Rectified octave-up voice — full-wave rectification doubles frequency for a fuzzy octave-up character; complex guitar and bass signals get wild in the best way Stank control — overload the octaving section on purpose for distortion blended with octave fuzz—a tone discovered during development, not an afterthought Blend — parallel mix from mostly dry (never fully dry) to fully wet Guitar and bass — responds to pickup output, playing dynamics, and signal complexity Hand-soldered in BC — true bypass, top-mounted jacks, LED brightness trim for outdoor stages Player-tested — Michael Schau demo below; same player community as the Crunch and Classic Fuzz lines How Stank works — the circuit The core circuit takes a relatively pure tone and doubles the frequency by inverting the positive portion of the wave—full-wave rectification. That yields a fuzzy octave-up sound. With the rich harmonic content of a guitar or bass, the result is aggressive, animated, and unpredictable in a musical way. During development we found that pushing too much signal through the octaving section didn’t just break up—it became positively “Stanky” (as one player put it). That happy accident became the Stank knob: think of it as distortion mixed with the octave-up fuzz, not a generic gain control. Quick voicing tip: With Stank up and Blend around 10 o’clock, it behaves like a distortion with octave overtones—useful for rhythm and chord work without full wet fuzz. Michael Schau demo Michael Schau taking the Octave Fuzz with Stank for a spin: ▶ All McGregor Pedals demos → Controls Vol — Output level. Turning up Stank can boost volume; adjust Vol as needed Stank — Overloads the octaving circuit—distortion blended with octave-up fuzz Blend — Wet/dry mix. Full left is mostly dry (it never fully dries up); full right is completely wet LED brightness — Side trim pot (jeweler’s screwdriver): dark stage to bright sun How to use it Starting point: Blend around noon, Stank low, set Vol to match your bypass level Octave fuzz: Bring Blend toward fully wet; add Stank to taste for filth vs. clarity Distortion + octave overtones: Stank up, Blend around 10 o’clock—rhythm-friendly voicing Bass: Works well on bass; complex low-end content drives the rectifier hard—start with lower Stank and adjust Blend Before Crunch: Stacks well with transparent overdrive after fuzz for cranked-amp textures at manageable volume Specifications Type: Rectified octave-up fuzz with overload Stank control (guitar & bass) Controls: Vol, Stank, Blend + LED brightness trim Bypass: True bypass Power: 9 V DC, center-negative 2.1 × 5.5 mm (Boss-style).
